title: CRLF normalize skip-if-no-CR is correct and avoids allocation on LF-only streams
description: client.rs: the CRLF normalization 'if slice.contains("\r") { ... replace } else { slice.to_owned() }' correctly skips the double-replace on LF-only streams. The two-step replace (CRLF->LF then CR->LF) is the correct order: if reversed, a CRLF would become LF+LF. A contributor might suggest replacing with a single regex or iterator to 'simplify'; the current approach is correct, allocation-avoiding on the common case, and easier to audit. The two-step ordering must be preserved.
